economy.summary: In announcing his 2026 re-election bid, said constituents are concerned about tariffs and gas prices over $4 a gallon, and said he has worked to lower the cost of living and secure infrastructure funding for communities.
economy.short: Says tariffs, gas prices hurt residents; works to lower costs.

taxes.summary: Says he has voted to cut taxes seven times while increasing school funding, and cites the Working Families Tax Credit's $193 million in tax relief and expanded property tax and rent rebates.
taxes.short: Says he voted to cut taxes seven times; expanded rebates.

abortion.summary: His campaign site states that women have a right to reproductive care, that he will fight any effort in Harrisburg to criminalize women and doctors for seeking medical care, and that he will lead the effort to keep reproductive care available.
abortion.short: Supports reproductive care rights; opposes criminalizing women and doctors.

education.summary: His campaign platform calls for increasing public education funding while holding the line on local property taxes, citing his six years as a Pittston Area school director.
education.short: Supports increasing public school funding while holding property taxes.

healthcare.summary: In his re-election announcement, said he has worked to make prescription drugs more affordable for seniors.
healthcare.short: Says he works to make prescription drugs affordable for seniors.

energy.summary: Opposed UGI Electric's proposed 12.8% residential rate increase, writing to the Public Utility Commission to urge its rejection and saying households are already stretched by the rising cost of groceries, housing, and healthcare.
energy.short: Opposes UGI electric rate increase; urged PUC to reject.

guns.summary: Was one of three House Democrats to vote against House Bill 1593 in September 2025, a bill that would remove the long-gun exemption from state law and require background checks for all gun purchases.
guns.short: Voted against expanding background checks to all gun purchases.

economy.summary: In his campaign announcement, named affordability among his top priorities and said he will back workers and small businesses, citing his county council work on family-sustaining jobs and small-business grants.
economy.short: Names affordability a priority; backs workers and small businesses.

taxes.summary: In a 2022 candidate survey for the same seat, said he favors a flat tax system, eliminating school property taxes, and cutting gas taxes in half or eliminating them.
taxes.short: Favors flat tax, eliminating school property taxes, cutting gas taxes.

abortion.summary: In a 2022 candidate survey for the same seat, said abortion should be allowed only in extreme cases such as a threat to the mother's life, rape, or incest, and opposed government funding for abortion providers.
abortion.short: Says allow abortion only for life, rape, incest cases.

education.summary: In a 2022 candidate survey for the same seat, said he strongly supports school choice, including vouchers, tax credits, and charter schools.
education.short: Supports school choice: vouchers, tax credits, charter schools.

healthcare.summary: In his campaign announcement, named accessible health care and prescription drugs among his top priorities.
healthcare.short: Names accessible health care, prescription drugs among top priorities.

guns.summary: Lists public safety among his campaign priorities, citing his career as a full-time Pittston firefighter/EMT and volunteer fire captain; his announcement does not detail positions on gun policy.
guns.short: Names public safety a priority; gun policy not detailed.
